page: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is an ARM-based burstable general-purpose virtual machine powered by AWS Nitro architecture. The instance provides 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores using the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, with single-threaded execution per core. It is allocated 32 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware acceleration for AES cryptographic operations. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no dedicated GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and offering a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded and memory-bound operations, juxtaposed with constrained single-thread throughput. Multi-core compute capabilities are reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 12,133.02 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,149.0, both scoring within the average tier. In practical workloads, it achieves solid throughput with 9.35 million Redis SET operations per second, 9.19 GB/s in static web serving, and competitive software compilation scores. However, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 877.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.11 GB/s. Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read speeds of 114.09 GB/s and write speeds of 53.44 GB/s.

The primary operational tradeoff of the t4g.2xlarge lies in its burstable CPU credit model. It provides efficient resource density and baseline multi-core throughput, making it cost-effective for intermittent processing demands. Sustained peak computation without sufficient accrued credits, however, will result in baseline throttling. The instance is suited for burstable web application backends, caching services, software build agents, microservices hosting, and mid-tier relational databases that experience cyclical utilization patterns.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is an ARM-based general-purpose instance featuring 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 32 GB of memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and provides a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance includes hardware AES support but omits local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmarks indicate balanced multi-core execution, delivering 9.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.19 GB/s static web serving, while single-thread instruction throughput remains limited. Because CPU utilization operates on a burstable credit schedule, the system offers an efficient cost profile for varying resource demands. It is well matched for mid-sized caching layers, microservices, continuous integration build jobs, and web applications that do not require uninterrupted maximum CPU utilization.
